name: Totalitarian democracy
summary: Totalitarian democracy, in J. L. Talmon's sense, is a form of popular-sovereignty politics that assumes one total truth and a predetermined harmonious order, treats all of life as political, and finds freedom in pursuing a collective purpose. Where the individual and the general will conflict, the state may coerce the individual, a logic Talmon traced from Rousseau through the Jacobin Terror and single-party dictatorship to communism.
scope: The Rousseau-Robespierre line as Talmon framed it in The Origins of Totalitarian Democracy (1952): Rousseau's general will, the Jacobin government of 1793-94 and its single-party dictatorship, with the extension to property as a secondary strand. Positions on topics those texts never address (modern technology, gender identity) are inferred and low-confidence. It excludes liberal democracy and fascism.

keyFigures.name: Jacob Leib Talmon
keyFigures.role: Historian who coined and developed the concept in The Origins of Totalitarian Democracy (1952).

keyFigures.name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
keyFigures.role: Author of The Social Contract, whose general will Talmon treats as the origin of the doctrine.

keyFigures.name: Maximilien Robespierre
keyFigures.role: Jacobin leader who defended terror as virtue in revolutionary government.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from Robespierre's aim of equality and protection of the people, which implies public provision for the needy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Jacobin concern that commerce serve public wealth rather than the enrichment of a few, which favours state intervention in wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Robespierre wants commerce to serve public wealth rather than 'immense riches to a few', and Talmon's model subordinates all spheres to a collective purpose, so markets are not trusted to decide.

public-ownership.rationale: Talmon's third stage extends total popular sovereignty to property, leading to communism, so major industries fall under common control.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Robespierre's republic of equality objects to 'immense riches' for a few, which supports heavy levies on large fortunes.

unions-good.rationale: Rousseau insists there be no partial society within the state because sectional bodies distort the general will; unions are inferred to be such bodies.

property-fundamental.rationale: The SEP reads Rousseau as treating individual rights, property included, as matters for the sovereign to decide, not as limits on it.

regulate-corporations.rationale: A state that treats economic life as a matter of the common good would tightly regulate large concerns; Robespierre warns against wealth concentrated in few hands.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian, communal emphasis; the sources do not discuss welfare programmes directly.

worker-ownership.rationale: The collective owner in this tradition is the whole political community, not the workers of each firm, so adherents are split or indifferent.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from Robespierre's demand for vigilance against internal enemies who are 'allies of those in the exterior'.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the virtue-centred view that government should 'purify manners' and not leave private vice alone.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Robespierre's condemnation of 'mercenary libellists' who discredit the people's cause and from the idea that opinion may be policed.

strong-leader.rationale: Rousseau allows a dictator in extremity who 'can do anything except make laws', and the Jacobin tradition accepted concentrated authority in a revolution.

state-harmful.rationale: The tradition holds that no sphere lies outside politics and that the state realizes the collective purpose, so it rejects the view that the state is harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Adherents split: Rousseau favours an armed citizen militia, while a revolutionary regime disarms suspected enemies.

empower-police-military.rationale: Robespierre calls terror 'justice prompt, severe and inflexible', which implies strong enforcement powers against enemies.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the emphasis on civic virtue and moral regeneration as public concerns.

rehabilitation.rationale: Robespierre defends severe, prompt justice against enemies of the republic and calls terror an emanation of virtue, not mild correction.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred; the Rousseauist republic relies on moral education and civic discipline starting in the family, though the sources do not discuss family forms.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the stress on enforced public morals, not from any text on the issue.

abortion-legal.rationale: The sources say nothing, and a virtue-minded state with pro-population concerns could go either way.

more-religion-public.rationale: Rousseau's civil religion, with dogmas the sovereign fixes, puts a state-prescribed belief in the centre of public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the commitment to enforced equality and from Robespierre's hostility to privilege.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; Rousseau treated sex roles as natural, though sources opened do not discuss it, so low.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Rousseau treats patriotic education as a primary duty of magistrates, forming citizens loyal to the community.

gradual-change.rationale: A perfectionist ideology aiming at a total, predetermined order rejects gradualism and trial and error; Robespierre calls for revolutionary government.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; the civic community is defined by commitment to the general will rather than ancestry, so adherents are indifferent.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from Rousseau's view that the sovereign is sole judge and cannot be bound by outside authority.

free-trade.rationale: Robespierre wants commerce to serve public wealth, and the planned collective purpose does not favour open trade.

nation-first.rationale: Patriotic loyalty to the political community is central, although the revolutionary strand also had universalist hopes.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Messianic democracy aspires to spread its truth; Robespierre links internal and external enemies, so exporting liberty is plausible.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred; a closed civic body bound to a common good sits badly with open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; Rousseau distrusted luxury but the tradition does not take a stand on growth limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from willingness to direct all areas of life collectively.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from the SEP account of Rousseau tracing inequality and dependence to technical advances such as metallurgy.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic and not tied to any principle of the ideology.

revolution-justified.rationale: Robespierre calls government in revolution 'the despotism of liberty against tyranny', and Talmon's second stage is revolutionary dictatorship.

experts-over-public.rationale: Sovereignty belongs to the people; the legislator only proposes laws for popular approval, although a guiding elite is accepted.

central-planning.rationale: Talmon's model has the state direct all spheres of life toward a single collective purpose, which in the economic sphere means planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The sources do not address market socialism; adherents are indifferent as long as the common good prevails.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the stress on equality against inherited privilege.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; a duty-centred republic is ambivalent about unconditional payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from the subordination of commerce to public wealth.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Talmon's account treats the state as director of all areas, economy included.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rousseau speaks of replacing natural inequality with a moral and legitimate equality, which favours broad distribution, though the sources do not specify small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Babeuvist strand of Talmon's story wants communism, but Rousseau and Robespierre keep property, so adherents split.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No position in the sources and no principle that decides it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Rousseau's ban on partial societies in the state cuts against state-recognised sectional bodies, though Jacobins also wanted class unity.

one-party-rule.rationale: Talmon's stage two is single-party dictatorship under a doctrine of total popular sovereignty, guided by one correct truth.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Robespierre sees weakness and prejudice as 'the road to monarchy' and sets the republic against kings.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents claim to be the true democracy, but hold that the general will can differ from what voters actually choose, so they do not accept bad choices.

direct-votes.rationale: Rousseau holds sovereignty cannot be represented, and that the English people are free only during elections.

workers-councils.rationale: The community as a whole, not a class body, is sovereign; sectional councils are partial associations.

right-to-secede.rationale: Sovereignty is a single, indivisible expression of the general will, so no part may withdraw from it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rousseau needs an extraordinary legislator and Jacobins cite virtue, but sovereignty remains with all citizens, so adherents split.

political-violence-never.rationale: Robespierre states terror, 'justice prompt, severe and inflexible', is justified against enemies of liberty.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from civic-republican admiration of martial virtue; not stated in the sources opened.

separate-church-state.rationale: Rousseau's civil religion lets the sovereign fix the dogmas of belief, and the SEP notes exclusion of those who reject them.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The civil religion is set by the sovereign and reason, not scripture; Rousseau cites a universal justice from reason.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Justice is the sovereign's function and private provision contradicts the idea that politics covers everything.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from Robespierre's picture of a republic threatened by allied foreign tyrants.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The community is formed by the social contract and general will, not by ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Talmon links Jacobinism to communism, but the Rousseauist core does not make class conflict the driver of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rousseau praises 'an equality that is moral and legitimate', and Robespierre makes equality central to the republic.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from the political community defined by its own contract rather than civilisation or religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Robespierre prefers morality to egotism and treats private interest as the road to corruption; Rousseau subordinates particular wills to the general will.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The SEP reads Rousseau as making rights matters of sovereign decision, and Talmon says the state must coerce the individual in conflict.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed as a political matter.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Rousseau criticised progress but the Jacobin tradition was modernising; adherents split.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The tradition wants order guided by a plan, not disruption for its own sake.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; a collective-purpose ideology would not leave bodily self-modification to individual freedom.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; the sovereign is the people's general will, not automated systems.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Talmon says all human action is political, with no sphere outside state purview.

restore-past-order.rationale: The ideology looks to a perfected future order, though Rousseau's Rome and Sparta are models, hence low.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Talmon contrasts totalitarian democracy, which applies an all-encompassing philosophy to politics, with the liberal pragmatic approach.

direct-action.rationale: Elections of the legislator and assemblies matter to Rousseau, though revolutionary mass action is accepted; low.

means-match-ends.rationale: Robespierre defends terror as the means to virtue, so the means need not resemble the end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Rousseau idealises early societies but does not advocate returning to foraging; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not stated; the state would still organise specialised roles.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Babeuvist communism says yes, the Rousseauist core does not; adherents split.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from the subordination of commerce to the public wealth.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not a thesis of the Rousseauist core; the Marxian strand would affirm it.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Talmon traces the line from Jacobin dictatorship to communism, and Robespierre's despotism of liberty is its forerunner.

taxation-theft.rationale: The sovereign holds authority over property and can decide what is useful to the community.

harm-principle.rationale: Talmon says liberalism recognises areas of life outside politics, totalitarian democracy does not.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The community and its general will, not the individual, hold primary standing in this tradition.

conscription.rationale: The patriotic duties of citizens to the community come first, which includes service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Participation in the general will is what makes citizens free; exit is not a safeguard.

state-as-business.rationale: The state serves a collective moral purpose, not customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Talmon locates freedom in pursuit of a collective purpose, not in absence of coercion, a positive conception.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources do not discuss it; this is a modern critique and not part of the tradition.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Rousseau's contract treats persons as equal, so inferred rejection.

organic-representation.rationale: Rousseau excludes partial societies and rejects representation of sovereignty.

total-state.rationale: Talmon says it recognises only the political plane and treats all human action as political.

national-rebirth.rationale: Robespierre speaks of regenerating the people through virtue and of purifying manners.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Revolutionary war had both defensive and liberating motives; adherents split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on the general will, not personal feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Rousseau rejects slavery and bondage as illegitimate, and Jacobins abolished feudal dues.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Talmon says adherents assume a single total truth, which they believe objectively knowable.

universal-morality.rationale: Rousseau states there is a universal justice emanating from reason alone.

single-common-good.rationale: Talmon calls it a single, total truth with a predetermined harmonious order; the general will is always right and tends to the public good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Anachronistic national question that the Rousseau-Jacobin texts never touch; no principle of the doctrine decides it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; citizenship in this tradition rests on joining the contract, which cuts neither way.

revive-national-language.rationale: Inferred: a doctrine that shapes citizens through common education and public culture would back a revived common language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; democracy in firms is not part of the tradition.

school-vouchers.rationale: Rousseau treats education as a primary duty of the state and wants it common to all.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred: a state directing the economy toward a collective purpose would not bind itself to balanced budgets.

economic-freedom.rationale: The ideology does not accept that political order rests on economic liberty, since the state directs the economy.

rule-by-example.rationale: Robespierre pairs virtue with terror and rejects virtue without force as impotent.

national-self-determination.rationale: Popular sovereignty applied to each nation is consistent with the tradition.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred; no outside body is above a sovereign people's judgment.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Rousseau and Robespierre both rely on reason but also on prescribed civil belief, so adherents split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the stress on the civic community.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from civic duty and virtue as the basis of the republic.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rousseau's no-partial-society principle and the single common good favour unity over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: A messianic regime may destroy old institutions, but Jacobin tradition also protected national heritage; no clear source.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; revolutionary France faced a coalition of monarchies but the sources do not state a bloc principle.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; the community is the nation of citizens, not a class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Rousseau held distinct roles but the sources opened do not discuss it and Jacobin views varied.

ban-interest.rationale: Not discussed; the doctrine subordinates economy to the public good but its texts never take up usury.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Equal civic membership under the general will excludes racial classification.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is the instrument of the general will, not of a class, in the Rousseauist core.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic and unconnected to the ideology.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from patriotic education forming citizens loyal to the community.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy thesis not found in the sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parties are partial associations that distort the general will.

national-mission.rationale: Talmon's messianic democracy sees itself as carrying a universal truth to humanity.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine denies sectional interests in the general will and Rousseau himself assumed distinct sex roles.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Robespierre denounces intriguers and corrupt factions who seek to replace each other.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Revolutionary justice is the regime's own tool; this is a liberal demand.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Talmon states totalitarian democracy extends politics over all of life.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts the equality of citizens before the general will.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Robespierre makes equality central, though enemies of the republic lose protection.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed by the Rousseau-Jacobin core.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources do not discuss settler states and the question splits the Jacobin and Marxian strands.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: One law for all citizens from the general will, with no sectional law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; the civil religion allows private belief but not rejection of civic dogma.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: religious dietary rules belong to private faith, while the civil religion's dogmas are set by the sovereign, not by a sectarian ban.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Rousseau demands patriotic education and civil religion but not scriptural instruction; split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Robespierre treats internal and external enemies as allies and defends strong revolutionary government.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The tradition grounds legitimacy in popular sovereignty, though consent means the general will, not individual votes.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred from subordinating commerce to public wealth, which fits mercantile state aims over open trade.

population-transfer.rationale: Not addressed; terror targeted individuals or factions.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Robespierre justifies terror against enemies of liberty.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The tradition values harmony and virtue over struggle between individuals.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Factions that seek to subvert the republic are to meet 'death in the very thought of a crime'.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Rousseau's freedom as obedience to self-given law is close; sources do not decide.

separated-powers.rationale: Sovereignty is single and indivisible; Talmon describes concentration in one party.

vanguard-party.rationale: Talmon's single party guided by the one truth resembles the vanguard idea, though Rousseau is not a source.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Equality and anti-riches stance of Robespierre.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Anachronistic; public property is favoured over transfer to individuals.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Sectional action would be suspect but the Marxian strand supports it; split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Rousseau blames social institutions and property for inequality.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Rousseau wants shared civic feeling, but the doctrine defines unity by creed and contract and not by ethnicity, so it is split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rousseau saw lot as suited to democracy in some conditions but chose elective aristocracy for government.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rousseau's dictator in extremity and Robespierre's revolutionary government justify suspension in danger.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The Jacobin economic policy in crisis; consistent with subordinating commerce to public welfare.

party-controls-media.rationale: Talmon's single party and total-truth premise imply controlled public opinion; Robespierre attacks libellists.

party-commands-army.rationale: A single party running the state with no separate sphere implies party command of the armed forces.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred: citizenship is bound to loyalty to the general will, which a long probation would test.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Virtue and equality imply modest officials; Robespierre called the Incorruptible.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party led by a single truth requires unity once adopted; factions are condemned.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sovereignty is inalienable and indivisible in Rousseau.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not directly addressed; the Jacobin Convention held executive power through committees.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Civil religion is set by the sovereign; the Jacobins subordinated clergy.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority belongs to the sovereign people and its general will, not clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Defence of the republic is a civic duty.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Rousseau gives the censorship the role of guarding public judgment and morals.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; Robespierre warned of decay into aristocracy.

recall-officials.rationale: Rousseau treats rulers as mere commissioners removable by the sovereign.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Revolutionary France fought coalitions but the sources do not address permanent alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine favours broad equal property under the community's authority but not a ban on renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Rousseau favours citizen militias, and the Jacobin levee en masse armed the nation.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rousseau praised simple rural virtue, though the sources opened do not detail it.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not discussed; the sources centre on citizen bodies, not on borders.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not discussed; the Jacobins relied on educated leaders, yet distrusted intellectual elites, so the doctrine is split.

death-penalty.rationale: Rousseau accepts death for the gravest crimes against the contract, and Robespierre defends severe justice.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine gives the state control of schooling but its texts do not address sex education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; reason and civil religion would be taught but not scripture.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Moral order is a public matter, inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Civic membership by contract rather than descent, inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: One common civic culture is favoured, inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The general law binds all and the civil religion is uniform.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Talmon says freedom lies in a collective purpose and the censorship shapes opinion.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: Talmon's third stage extends popular sovereignty to property, so political change is incomplete without economic change.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Founding by an assembly of the people fits popular sovereignty, though the legislator proposes laws.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Talmon says freedom is pursuing a collective purpose, so temporary restriction for aims is acceptable.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not discussed; universalist liberty talk is balanced by loyalty to one's own republic.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred: a sovereign unbound by outsiders would keep its own arms, though the topic is anachronistic.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; Rousseau favoured elective aristocracy for government.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Anachronistic; the sovereign should control economic power.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Rousseau treats property as held under the community's authority and rights as matters for the sovereign, and the common good guides all.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Talmon's line from Jacobinism to communism treats the Soviet state as its heir.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred: a state directing every area of life would favour acting before risks are certain.

collective-defense.rationale: Not discussed; a sovereign people decides for itself, which both supports and opposes binding pacts.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Rousseau's civil religion places belief under the sovereign.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The ruling truth is partisan in the sense of single-party rule.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: An indivisible sovereign people may defend its unity, inferred from the general will.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine-descent rulers contradict popular sovereignty and the republic against kings.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Equality and anti-riches favour progressive levies.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic and unconnected to any principle in the sources.

character-from-environment.rationale: Rousseau holds institutions and education shape the citizen, requiring a legislator.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The sovereign is the people, which makes laws and is unbound, while rulers are bound; split.

leader-cult.rationale: The Cult of the Supreme Being existed but public cult of persons is not endorsed in the sources.

equal-parenting.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine treats the family as a matter for the state's moral order, giving no answer on custody.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not addressed by the Rousseau-Jacobin core.

land-redistribution.rationale: Equality and anti-concentration, inferred, Babeuvist strand explicit but unopened.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The political community is not ethnic, inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Rousseau punishes false profession of civil religion by death but leaves private belief free; split.

women-must-cover.rationale: Anachronistic and not part of the tradition.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from the sovereign's inalienable control of its own economy.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from civic rather than kin-based community.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from a single sovereign and no partial societies.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Talmon's Marxist stage says yes, the Rousseau-Jacobin core does not.

ban-cartels.rationale: Concentrations of economic power are opposed by Robespierre's critique of immense riches.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred to be split: state direction favours rescuing firms of public importance, yet Robespierre opposes enriching a few.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The general will is sovereign and not to be limited by institutions; Talmon notes the state may coerce.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Anachronistic; equality is central but sectional quotas conflict with a single general will.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from subordinating commerce to public wealth and the state's direction of the economy.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine's regard for external binding rules is low but standards fit its moral aims.

moral-incentives.rationale: Robespierre makes virtue the basis of popular government.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from willingness to use revolutionary means; Jacobin clubs acted without waiting for conditions.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Robespierre sets the republic of equality against monarchy and aristocracy.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rousseau's legislator tutors a people, but sources do not address rule over other societies.

patriotic-education.rationale: Rousseau treats education as a primary duty to form patriotic citizens loyal to the general will.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic; equality is central but the doctrine accepts state action to enforce it, so it is split.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from public control of economic life.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not discussed; the Marxian strand denies it and the Rousseauist core never addresses it.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not discussed; inferred state control of trade could support it but sources are silent.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; a Marxist-Leninist debate foreign to the Jacobin core.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: No sphere of private life outside the political purpose, and equality is central.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights are matters of sovereign decision, not limits on it.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rousseau proposes elective aristocracy for administration; Robespierre republican.

minority-veto.rationale: The general will binds all, with the dissenter forced to be free.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Rousseau treats government as commissioners the sovereign may remove.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Sovereign is the people, which does not delegate legislation to parliament.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Rousseau argued animals share sentience; the opened sources do not state it, so low.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternal privilege contradicts equality; rights not charity.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Talmon says all human action is political.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not discussed; Rousseau criticised theatre and the arts but the opened sources do not address it.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not discussed; civic virtue and loyalty count more than birth in the doctrine.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: patriotic self-sufficiency and sovereignty against outside dependence.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: one sovereign people with no partial societies denies group-based claims to leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine predates fascism and Talmon places both movements as heirs of the same premises.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Talmon's thesis itself links these, but adherents would not call themselves totalitarian; split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anachronistic and not tied to any principle in the sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: a regime that fixes public truth and honours its own heroes would remove symbols of the old order.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The tradition claims a universal truth.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Rousseau's dictator is civil; Jacobins subordinated army to the Convention.

paid-care-work.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not discussed; Rousseau favours election of officials and virtue over examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from state direction of strategic economic life.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Anachronistic; the Jacobins legalised divorce in 1792 but the sources opened do not show the doctrine's stance.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Rousseau says deputies are only commissioners who cannot conclude anything definitively.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Individual market accounts conflict with collective purposes; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The community holds the ultimate title, per SEP's reading of property under the sovereign.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not discussed; the sovereign people, not parliament, controls the purse in Rousseau's scheme.

single-official-language.rationale: A single common culture is a unifying device, inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the community holds ultimate authority over land and citizenship is tied to loyalty.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic; equality is central but the doctrine has no view on this legal test.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Robespierre prefers morality to egotism; Rousseau linked luxury with corruption.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's messianic export of its truth and Robespierre's link between internal and external enemies.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not discussed; a messianic power might intervene but the sources are silent.

corporate-influence.rationale: Robespierre objects to wealth and intriguers capturing the republic.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign allies of internal enemies were Robespierre's concern.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: a state directing all areas of life, with Rousseau's concern for citizen numbers, would back incentives.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the state directing the economy for the common good.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not discussed; Talmon's messianic democracy sees war with enemies of the revolution as likely.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The social contract binds all, and the dissenter is forced to be free.

non-intervention.rationale: Messianic universalism would not accept strict non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not discussed; unions are sectional bodies the doctrine distrusts.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Robespierre's factions are political, not ethnic; sources do not endorse ethnic conspiracies.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not discussed; public opinion matters, but a regime of single truth controls the information.

informal-organisation.rationale: Rousseau rejects partial societies, and unified party discipline is required.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The sovereign is sole judge and not bound externally.

religious-nation.rationale: Civil religion but political, not tied to a religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: popular sovereignty rejects ritual submission to a foreign power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: A unitary sovereign pools resources, inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: Talmon links Jacobinism to communism; adherents unspecific.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public services belong to the state.

religion-illusion.rationale: Rousseau and Robespierre kept a civil religion; Marxian strand disagrees; split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not addressed; the Marxian strand yes, Rousseau no.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not discussed; the Marxian strand agrees, the Rousseauist core does not address it.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Rousseau-type sovereign is one civic body, not many small communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not discussed; a unitary republic might encourage uniformity but the sources do not say.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Talmon links Jacobinism to communism; adherents do not seek a third course.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The tradition says nothing on this; a regime claiming one total truth based on reason would reject denial, inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic; the Jacobin era decriminalised it in 1791 but the sources opened are silent.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Talmon's single party dictatorship and Robespierre on factions imply suppression of opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Rousseau's civil religion punishes public bad faith with death.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: legitimacy comes from the general will, not religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct popular sovereignty is Rousseau's ideal.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic; not part of the doctrine's analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The tradition is a single total truth rather than a mixture.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxian theme, which Talmon places in the third stage, but the core texts never state it.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Foreign to the tradition; its civil religion has no stated view on Islam.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority comes from the people's general will, per Rousseau.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from a uniform civic order.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Talmon says this ideology treats the whole economy as political, not a market with safeguards.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Robespierre's republic faces armed enemies and Rousseau favours citizen arms.

rich-first.rationale: Equality is central and large riches are condemned.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not discussed; Robespierre's republic faced coalitions, so neutrality was no choice.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: the sovereign is sole judge of its own policy and external conditions limit it.

property-franchise.rationale: The people as a whole are sovereign.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Robespierre condemns hired libellists; wealth distorts public opinion.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rousseau holds law is a general will expressed in general rules, not particular decrees.

racial-franchise.rationale: All citizens take part in the general will.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: the civil religion is a shared creed for all, with no basis for sectarian marriage law.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Rousseau prefers assemblies of all citizens, not selected samples.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not discussed; the sovereign fixes the civil dogmas, but their meaning is not given.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Robespierre says commerce should not merely enrich a few and warns of decay into aristocracy.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Robespierre and Rousseau kept a civil religion rather than atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Terror as swift justice is endorsed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: A single general will leaves no room for communal division.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the public duty to the poor.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from Robespierre's fear of decay into aristocracy and Rousseau's commissioners removable at will.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; Rousseau rejects representation, though delegation differs.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not discussed; the civil religion has no clergy hierarchy in Rousseau.

decide-locally.rationale: Sovereignty is one and indivisible and the general will is national, so local decision-making is subordinated.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A unitary sovereign and single legal order, inferred from indivisible general will.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not addressed; the property question is left to the sovereign in this tradition.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Rousseau's citizenship as membership in the sovereign body bound by the social contract, which gives political voice to citizens only.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Rousseau's and Robespierre's wish to limit inequality of wealth so none is rich enough to buy another, which favours state limits on property.

abolish-ip.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; the sources give no basis for either side.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from Rousseau's civic education that forms citizens for the general will and the Jacobin aim of shaping virtuous patriots; uniforms and drill themselves are not stated.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from Rousseau's sovereign people that cannot be subject to outside will, so foreign military presence is hard to square with popular sovereignty.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; no basis in the sources for either side.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Robespierre treats property as a social institution to be limited by equality, and Rousseau wants no citizen rich enough to buy another, so wealth is subordinate to the public good.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Robespierre defends terror as inflexible justice and Rousseau allows death for the enemies of the state, so killing in defence of the republic is not wrong.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the Jacobin project of regenerating the people and breaking with the old order rather than affirming ancient continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed by Talmon's line; Rousseau treats sex differences as natural, so a constructionist view is unlikely.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from Rousseau's fixed natural roles for women; modern feminist debate is anachronistic here.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the Jacobin cult of virtue and civil religion, which honours those who die for the fatherland; honouring them as saints is not stated.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Robespierre frames politics as the struggle of virtue against vice and Rousseau's civil religion gives the state a sacred creed, matching Talmon's total-truth thesis.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from the single sovereign people gathered in one state under one general will, not a homeland serving a dispersed diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from Rousseau's Legislator and the Jacobin republic, where institutions and state-led education form the people rather than culture preceding the state.

god-not-male.rationale: Rousseau's civil religion and Robespierre's Supreme Being are deist and do not address gendered language for God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; the civil religion has no scripture to judge, and women's humanity is not the test applied to religion.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the universalist citizenship of the Jacobin republic, which resists ethnic-majority economic claims, though foreign and factional enemies are suspect.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The Jacobin republic was one and indivisible and suppressed provincial particularities, so merging regions for a particular people runs against it.

independent-unions.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Talmon's point that all of life is political and a single general will leaves no autonomous organisation apart from the state.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Jacobin aim that the people itself holds power and from the secondary property strand, which subordinates property to the common good.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Robespierre's view that the state must secure the people's subsistence and welfare.

second-chamber.rationale: Rousseau holds sovereignty indivisible and the general will undivided, and the Jacobin regime ran through a single Convention and committees, so a rival chamber has no place.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the general will and its central government decide on property, leaving no independent local ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The Jacobins treated federalism as treason against the one and indivisible Republic, and the general will is one and central, so local assemblies keeping decisions is rejected.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Robespierre's draft that society owes subsistence to citizens and from Rousseau's traditional family.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The tradition is indifferent to drug regulation; no principle points either way.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The tradition is indifferent to ageing research; no principle points either way.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the totalising state that polices suspects and claims all of life as political, which would not tolerate untraceable transactions.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Terror's surveillance of suspects and the demand that citizens publicly show virtue and loyalty.

person-over-state.rationale: Talmon's central charge is that the general will may force individuals, who are 'forced to be free', so persons are means to the collective purpose; the Social Contract states this directly.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Rousseau's civil religion and Robespierre's Supreme Being worship treat civic and moral virtue as spiritual ends of politics.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The Jacobin Republic was unitary and any local authority was delegated and supervised from the centre, so regional powers would be revocable.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; the tradition has no bearing on agricultural technology.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic; the tradition has no bearing on urban form.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from a single general will of the whole people and universal citizenship, which leaves no room for rival group interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from Jacobin civic universalism, which grounded pride in the Republic and virtue rather than ancestry.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred: the Jacobin Republic waged revolutionary war and exported its principles, so a defensive-only rule does not fit, though Robespierre doubted aggressive war early on.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Rousseau-Jacobin line defined the nation by the general will of citizens, though Jacobin policy also pressed French linguistic unity; no clear stance on language-based nations.

communal-electorates.rationale: Rousseau holds that partial associations must not stand between citizen and the general will, so separate community electorates are rejected.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Robespierre's 1794 speech and Jacobin rule rest on the claim that foreign tyrants and internal agents conspire against the republic.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed in these sources; inferred from the Jacobin aim of public education forming citizens, which implies state-funded schooling.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources give no basis for a position on environmental taxation.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Robespierre's language of founding a republic that endures for posterity.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the single general will, which gives no group weight on the basis of distinct values; Rousseau separately assigned women a domestic role.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from the Jacobin war footing and levee en masse, which treated armed strength as essential to defending the revolution.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Jacobins denounced secret royal diplomacy, but the Terror-era Committee of Public Safety conducted foreign policy confidentially; the sources give no stated position.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from Robespierre's wish for commerce to serve public wealth and for strong state control of the economy in the emergency.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: A sovereign general will with no rival power centres implies the state alone commands force; inferred from the Jacobin centralised government.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Rousseau and Robespierre demand citizens' devotion to the patrie in arms, so refusal of orders in inter-state wars is inferred to be rejected.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Rousseau warns that partial associations distort the general will and should be prevented, which tells against independent unions bargaining.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The revolutionary government acts for the general will without external limits, so fixed legal borrowing limits are inferred to be unwelcome.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: International economic rules were outside Talmon's account and the sources.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Jacobin revolutionary government centralised and used the state machinery for virtue and terror rather than smashing it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Talmon's model assumes one predetermined harmonious order, so competing economic experiments are the opposite of its premise.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; Rousseau and Robespierre never discussed ecosystem accounting.

sacred-nation.rationale: Rousseau's civil religion and Robespierre's cult of the Supreme Being sanctify the fatherland and demand citizens' lives be devoted to it.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic for the 1790s strand.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The strand takes a unitary nation-state and treats regional particularity as faction; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Rousseau's legislator is to change human nature, transforming individuals into parts of a greater whole, so a fixed nature that should not be redesigned is rejected.

public-service-media.rationale: Independence from government is incompatible with a state that finds freedom in a collective purpose and rejects dissent; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Talmon's model assumes one total truth, and Rousseau's civil religion accepts only faiths compatible with its dogmas; inferred at low confidence.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from Robespierre's concern that property and commerce serve the people's welfare.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the emphasis on the state's strength and sovereignty against rivals.

workers-own-party.rationale: Rousseau bars partial societies and factions that stand between citizen and the general will, and Robespierre attacks factions, so an independent class party is disfavoured.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the readiness to coerce individuals and customs in the name of the general will.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Rousseau and the Jacobins did not treat women as equal citizens, yet equality of property was a Jacobin concern; no direction is clear.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from the Jacobin drive for a single national language and unity, which treated regional tongues as local dialects.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the preference for public authority over private litigation for protecting the common good.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from Rousseau's rejection of intermediary bodies between citizen and sovereign, which would exclude a chiefly advisory role.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the principle that the general will overrides individual liberty when they conflict.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the Jacobin belief in virtue backed by terror and in strict, uniform law against enemies of the people.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the Jacobin ideal of a unified citizenry sharing common purpose and civic culture.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Unions are not addressed; inferred from Rousseau's ban on partial associations and the single general will, which leaves no room for voluntary sectional bodies, so compulsion into collective bodies fits better than a right to opt out.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Rousseau's view that only citizens form the sovereign, which implies the state may verify who is a citizen.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Rousseau's civil religion has dogmas fixed by the sovereign and bans intolerance of them, so the state does privilege one creed over others.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Talmon's thesis is that popular sovereignty serving a single predetermined purpose is democratic in name only, and that procedure without that purpose is not the test.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed by Robespierre; inferred from Rousseau's view that public virtue and austere morals govern private conduct, and his conservative view of women's role.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Robespierre's defence of emergency coercion in the name of public safety and the people's survival.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Robespierre's preference for public provision and a right to subsistence over cash payments that rely on market earnings.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from Rousseau's exclusion of women from public life and the Jacobin closure of women's political clubs.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Robespierre and Rousseau treating religion (civil religion, Supreme Being) as a source of civic morality rather than oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Jacobin doctrine of one indivisible people of equal citizens, which treats ancestry as irrelevant to political standing.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Rousseau's view of separate spheres for women and men, which leaves no place for agencies to promote equality.

missingStatements.text: Citizens who profess a state creed but act as though they do not believe it should be put to death.
missingStatements.rationale: Rousseau's civil religion chapter prescribes death for hypocrisy before the law, the clearest enforcement of the creed.
missingStatements.declined: Extreme and specific to Rousseau's civil religion; punish-blasphemy and suppress-opposition cover the contested ground.

missingStatements.text: Government in a revolution may rule by terror against enemies of liberty.
missingStatements.rationale: Robespierre calls terror justice prompt, severe and inflexible, an emanation of virtue.

notes: Totalitarian democracy is an analytic label from Talmon, not a self-description; adherents here are modelled on the Rousseauist-Jacobin doctrine. A Marxist strand would answer property and class questions differently.
